long_biography.plain_text:
An employee's prototype for a small business-phone device drew Norman Worthington back from semi-retirement and into his eighth technology start-up. He and Star2Star president Joseph Rhem tested the concept in a garage, developing a system that routed office communications over internet links while retaining equipment at customers' sites.

Worthington's earlier software ventures had produced consumer programs including Mavis Beacon Teaches Typing and the Chessmaster series. He also co-founded the mobile dictation business CopyTalk and participated in a Computer Associates joint venture behind the Opal integration system. At Star2Star, he remained close to product development, appearing as a co-inventor on communications-network patents before becoming chairman of Sangoma after its acquisition of the company.
